mission.display_title: Form marginal and conditional distributions from a joint
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to turn a joint distribution into marginal and conditional distributions (so you can obtain the probability/density function for one variable alone and for one given the other) without pretending independence or covariance LOs are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to obtain a marginal and a conditional from a stated joint. And refuse treating 'I wrote a joint table' as having the marginal or conditional.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from joint statement to lawful marginal and conditional distributions.
mission.learning_objective: Obtain the probability function or density function for marginal and conditional distributions of jointly distributed random variables.
mission.concept_focus: Joint → marginal (sum/integrate) → conditional (normalise by marginal) → refuse joint-as-margins-done.
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Gamma closed univariate evaluation and generation (2.1) with Revision. Today opens topic 2.2 at LO 2.2.1. The named Continuity Front after CS1-004.
mission.why_now: Joint distributions start here: pull marginals and conditionals from a joint so independence and dependence work have a base.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to extract a named marginal and conditional from a joint table by actual computation, not recognition alone.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Epsilon Day 1 because CE-001 / EP-001 Continuity Front names 2.2 as the handoff from Gamma.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly obtains marginal and conditional distributions from a joint distribution?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Marginalisation removes the other variable by summation or integration. Conditioning renormalises by the conditioning event's marginal.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Marginal: sum or integrate out the other variable. Conditional: joint divided by conditioning marginal.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating a joint entry as a finished marginal or conditional without the required operation.

choices.label: Obtain a marginal by summing or integrating the joint distribution over the other variable. Obtain a conditional by dividing the relevant joint probability or density by the marginal of the conditioning value.
The joint distribution is already numerically equal to every marginal and conditional, so no extraction or normalisation is needed.
Obtain a marginal by dividing each joint value by the other variable, and obtain a conditional by summing over the conditioning variable.
A conditional probability equals its joint numerator without division whenever the joint table totals one.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Joint PMF: P(0,0)=0.10, P(0,1)=0.20, P(1,0)=0.30, P(1,1)=0.40. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute one marginal and one conditional probability.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Sum the X=1 row for the marginal, then divide the (1,1) cell by that row total.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using a single joint cell as a marginal or failing to normalise a conditional.

choices.label: P(X=1)=0.40 because the largest cell in the X=1 row is the marginal.
P(Y=1|X=1)=0.40 because the joint cell is already conditional.
P(X=1)=0.70 and P(Y=1|X=1)=0.60 because P(Y=1) is the conditional numerator.
